newsitem.title: CHINA: China Jan-July foreign funds rise 35 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: China Jan-July foreign funds rise 35 pct yr/yr.

text.p: China's contracted foreign funds totalled $53.52 billion in January-July, an increase of 35.2 percent compared with the same period last year, the China Information said on Friday.
Direct foreign investment reached $48.52 billion during the first seven months, up 31.7 percent over the year-ago period, the newspaper quoted figures from the State Statistical Bureau as showing.
Actual foreign funds used rose four percent in the period to $26.81 billion, the newspaper said.
Foreign loans totalled $4.78 billion, a rise of 100 percent compared with the year-ago period, it said.
Contracted funds for solely foreign-invested projects jumped 55.1 percent to $18.44 billion while funds for joint ventures rose 35.2 percent year-on-year, it said.
Investment in cooperative projects slipped by 8.6 percent, it said without giving further details.
The report attributed the rises in part to Beijing's efforts to attract more investment to primary and secondary industries.

Contracted foreign funds in those industries in the first six months of the year had accounted for 77.7 percent of total foreign investment in the period, up by 15.7 percentage points compared with the same period in 1995, it said.
Overseas investors had poured more funds into more remote and backward western and central areas, with investment in those areas growing at more than 50 percent in the first half, it said.
